title: HVAC Systems Troubleshooting Essentials
summary: Hands-on troubleshooting skills for CRAC/CRAH systems and common cooling failures.
description: Built for technicians who need practical troubleshooting skills, not design theory. This course covers refrigeration cycle fundamentals, psychrometrics basics, and hands-on CRAC/CRAH diagnostics — the skills you use during an actual cooling failure, not just a scheduled inspection. You'll work through common failure modes, airflow measurement techniques, and a preventive maintenance schedule you can apply immediately, plus emergency troubleshooting procedures for when cooling capacity drops unexpectedly.
why_it_matters: When a cooling unit fails in a data hall, temperatures can rise quickly, especially in high-density rows. The technician on site needs to find the cause fast: a failed compressor, a refrigerant problem, a stuck valve, a bad sensor or a controls issue. Guessing and swapping parts wastes time the room does not have. Effective troubleshooting starts with the refrigeration cycle and the numbers that describe it, such as pressures, superheat and subcooling, plus enough psychrometrics to understand dew point and humidity. It also means knowing the difference between direct-expansion CRAC units and chilled-water CRAH units. This course covers refrigeration cycle fundamentals, CRAC/CRAH diagnostics, common failures and maintenance practices that prevent repeat problems.
audience: HVAC technicians working on data center cooling equipment.
prerequisites: No prior certification required. Relevant equipment exposure is helpful.
learning_outcomes: Diagnose common CRAC/CRAH failure modes quickly and accurately
Apply refrigeration cycle fundamentals to real troubleshooting scenarios
Measure airflow correctly to identify cooling distribution problems
Build a preventive maintenance schedule that reduces emergency callouts

faqs.question: What are superheat and subcooling?
faqs.answer: Superheat is how much the refrigerant vapor temperature is above its boiling point at the evaporator outlet. Subcooling is how much the liquid is below its condensing temperature at the condenser outlet. Together they help diagnose charge problems, restrictions and valve issues.

faqs.question: Why does humidity matter in a data center?
faqs.answer: High humidity can cause condensation and corrosion, while very low humidity increases static discharge risk. ASHRAE's thermal guidelines give recommended ranges based on dew point and relative humidity, and cooling units must be tuned to stay within them.

faqs.question: Is this a design course?
faqs.answer: No. It is built for technicians who need practical diagnostic skills. For system design and optimization, see Cooling Systems Design & Optimization.
